rows: Health professional’s conclusions and working assumptions that will guide treatment of the patient.

Actor that created or revised the data.

Usage note: The actor may be a provider, a patient, a device, an outside medical record, or something else. The source of the information can be used to form assessments about its quality, reliability, trustworthiness, or can indicate where to go to determine the origins of the information.

Category of actor that participated in the creation or revision of data.

Usage note: The source of the information can be used to form assessments about its quality, reliability, trustworthiness, or can indicate where to go to determine the origins of the information.

Examples include but are not limited to provider, patient, family member, and device.
Date and time of author action.

Sequence of characters used to uniquely refer to a member of the care team. Examples include but are not limited to National Provider Identifier (NPI) and National Council of State Boards of Nursing Identifier (NCSBN ID).
Place where care is delivered by a care team member. Examples include but are not limited to clinic address, and location description.
Word or phrase that constitutes the distinctive designation of a care team member. Examples include but are not limited to given name, middle name, surname, and name suffix.
Responsibility of an individual within the care team. Examples include but are not limited to primary care physician and caregiver.
Phone or email contact information for a care team member.
Place where a person is located or may be contacted.
Known or estimated year, month, and day of the patient's birth.
Known or estimated year, month, and day of the patient's death.
Unique identifier of an individual's email account that is used to send and receive email messages.
Patient's self-identification as Hispanic/ Latino or Non- Hispanic/ Non-Latino.
A personal name used before a family name.
Portion of one's personal name indicating familial or communal ties.
A second or subsequent given name, between the first given name and the family name or surname.
Name component following family name that may be used to describe a person's position in a family.
Numbers and symbols to contact an individual when using a phone.
Any first and last name an individual may have used in the past for any reason.
An individual’s response to the race question based upon self-identification.
Documentation of a specific instance of sex.
Date of first determination by a qualified professional of the presence of a problem or condition affecting a patient.
Date of subsiding or termination of a symptom, problem or condition.
Supporting evidence that is the basis for determining the condition.
Condition, diagnosis, or reason for seeking medical attention.
The genetic makeup of an individual's blood group, specifically the blood type and Rh factor.
The categorical or clinical assessment of the genetic variant data, where interpretation is necessary to fully understand the significance.
Amount of a medication for each administration.
Pharmacologic agent used in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of disease.
Physical location of available services or resources.
Sequence of characters representing a physical place of available services or resources.
Word or words by which a facility is known.

Category of service or resource available in a location.

Examples include but are not limited to hospital, laboratory, pharmacy, ambulatory clinic, long-term and post-acute care facility, and food pantry.
Analysis of specimens derived from humans which provide information for the diagnosis, prevention, treatment of disease, or assessment of health.
Documented findings of a tested specimen including structured and unstructured components
